description: Verify that DUT silently discards an ICMP message whose `type` field is unknown to the implementation (RFC 1122 §3.2.2 MUST) — unknown types must not produce any reply or visible side-effect
approach:
[Objective]
Unknown ICMP types are forward-compatibility space — newer specs may define them. Today's implementation must drop them silently rather than guess at meaning or generate spurious responses.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ICMP message
   • type        = some value not in the implementation's recognised set (e.g. 99)
   • addressed to DUT

2. Observation (5 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: nothing — no ICMP traffic of any kind

[Pass condition]
DUT does not emit any ICMP message within the observation window.

[Fail condition]
Fail_dut_replied — DUT emitted some ICMP response (any type) to the unknown-type message. Indicates the receive path doesn't gate on known-type list.

verdicts.Pass: DUT silently discarded the unknown ICMP type — normal
verdicts.Fail_dut_replied: DUT emitted a response to an unknown ICMP type — type filter missing
